dataset.cohort_definition: Validation encounters with at least one message at or above the 2-day cutoff whose final message is inside 2 days (final_is_early excluded, decision D4). all_usable also includes final_is_early encounters.

thresholds.selection: 5-fold out-of-fold on training partition, primary cohort

rankings.label: Time to closest approach, soonest first

test.reason: Test messages include current risk and have no final outcomes.

limitations: Validation partition only (one saved split, seed 42). test_data.csv has no outcomes, so no test metrics exist.

The upgrade threshold was chosen by ML (D7) on 5-fold out-of-fold predictions from the training partition, then applied to a model refitted on the whole partition. The 25% upgrade-precision budget therefore does not transfer exactly, and it was checked on the same scores it was tuned on.
The D7 budget is a trade-off constraint. Persistence has one operating point, so the two models are not compared at an equal false-alarm level.
p_critical is an uncalibrated, class-weighted score for 'final tier is Critical'. It is not a collision probability (Pc) and is shown only as ranking quality.
Critical support is small (126 primary validation encounters), so intervals are wide.
Encounters with no eligible early message are unable to assess. They are excluded from tier metrics and counted separately, never as Safe.

notes: train_event_labels.csv bytes differ from split_meta.json (for example a local export of the organiser sheet). Its content is cross-checked row by row against raw messages and the split.

d7_constraint.note: A trade-off budget (at most 3 false alarms per extra Critical caught), enforced on training out-of-fold predictions. It is not evidence of a comparable false-alarm level.

uncertainty.method: paired bootstrap over encounters, 2000 resamples, seed 42, percentile 95% interval

primary.headline: Primary validation cohort: at its fixed threshold the upgrade model catches 110 of 126 Critical encounters vs 101 for persistence (+9; paired 95% CI of the recall gain +0.029 to +0.118). False Critical alarms rise from 31 to 52 (false-positive rate 1.9% to 3.1% of 1660 non-Critical encounters); 30 upgrades, upgrades correct 30% (D7 budget 25% on training folds). This is a trade-off, not an equal-false-alarm comparison.

tradeoff_curve.note: Descriptive only. Computed on validation after the threshold was fixed; not used for selection.

all_usable.headline: All-usable validation cohort: at its fixed threshold the upgrade model catches 151 of 167 Critical encounters vs 142 for persistence (+9; paired 95% CI of the recall gain +0.024 to +0.089). False Critical alarms rise from 31 to 55 (false-positive rate 1.4% to 2.5% of 2222 non-Critical encounters); 33 upgrades, upgrades correct 27% (D7 budget 25% on training folds). This is a trade-off, not an equal-false-alarm comparison.
